# OCG Session Head (@verneuil/dsh-ocg-session-head)
**Injects a per-conversation `x-opencode-session` request header for OpenCode Go routes**
[](README.md) [](README.zh.md)
Changelog · Issues

> ### ⚠️ Read this first: if either condition below does not apply, you do not need this plugin
>
>

**1) Your host must be DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2 or newer**
>
> The plugin does exactly one thing: it w

rites a header inside the header seat the host officially provides
> (the `llm-pi-ai/request-headers

` waterfall). That seat only appeared in **0.2.2-alpha.3** and became stable
> in 0.2.2-rc.1 — **old

er versions simply do not have this foundation**. Installing it on an older host does
> not error ou

t, but it **never takes effect** — it looks like “installed but useless”, when in fact there is
> no

where for it to hook into.
>
> **2) It only matters for OpenCode connected under a custom provider n

ame**
>
> - If you added OpenCode / OpenCode Go through DSH's **official path** (using pi-ai's built

-in
>   `opencode` / `opencode-go` routes), recent pi-ai already adds the session header **automatic

ally** —
>   **you do not need this plugin**, and installing it is pure redundancy.
> - Only when yo

u connect like this — **you really do use an OpenCode service, but the provider name is your
>   own
** (a hand-written `baseURL` plus `api: openai-completions`, say you call it `ocg`) — is that automa

tic
>   wrapping out of reach, and this plugin is what supplies the header.
>
> In one sentence: **o
fficial path → no plugin needed; custom name → use this plugin.**

## 1. Why it is needed
Since 2026-09-05, OpenCode Go requires every inference request to carry a stable `x-opencode-session

`,
otherwise it returns:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
pi-ai already wraps the **built-in** `opencode` / `opencode-go` routes; but a **custom-named** route
(your own name, hand-written `baseURL` + `api: openai-completions`) never gets that wrapping, so a

plugin has
to supply the header.
> Not sure which case you are? See item 2 of “Read this first” above.
## 2. Version requirements (important)
| Item | Requirement |
| DSH | **≥ 0.2.2** (the `llm-pi-ai/request-headers` seat arrived in 0.2.2-alpha.3; available from t

he 0.2.2 line) |
| Node | No extra requirement (pure ESM, zero dependencies) |
Installing on an **older** host is safe: the plugin loads and logs its ready line, but the event nev

er
fires → behaviour equals not installing it (OCG still returns 400). **This makes “install first,

upgrade
later” a valid step-by-step verification path.**

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `providers` | `['ocg']` | Provider-key allowlist, matched exactly against `provider` in the event

|

### Config validation (errors are loud)
Following the official “misconfiguration should be loud” principle, **an invalid config fails plugin
activation and names the offending field** — it never falls back silently.
| Situation | Behaviour |

| Key not set (`undefined`) | Default is used |
| Unknown key (likely a typo) | ❌ Error, valid keys

listed |

## 9. Known limitations
- Only **pi-ai routes** are covered (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`). `deepseek-official` goes through
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek`, which sends its own `x-deepseek-harness-session-id` and is unrelat

ed.
- **Model discovery is not covered** (the host contract explicitly says the event `excludes mode

l discovery`).
- The event is **synchronous**: a listener must mutate `headers` in place and `return

next()` immediately, and
must not retain the object reference.
- `engines.dsh` is declared as `>=0.

2.2-alpha.3`. The host evaluates compatibility with
`includePrerelease: true`, so a plain `>=0.2.2`

would reject `0.2.2-rc.1`, and `>=0.2.2-rc.1` would reject a
future `0.2.3-rc.1`. Anchoring at the a

lpha that introduced the header seat accepts both the stable line and
every later RC, while anything
below `0.2.2` is correctly rejected.
